references.title: Steerable Technic front axle; the pinion lives in the parent

discovery.description: Steerable front axle assembly with suspension arms, shock absorber, steering rack, and steering links.

notes.lesson: A steerable, sprung Technic front axle carries the steering rack, but the 8T pinion that drives the rack is placed in the parent frame.
notes.construction: 29 parts in 11 source steps. Step 6: suspension arms pivot on a 1×6 Technic brick, with towball ends. Step 9: the shock absorber. Step 10: two `8081 - Front Axle S10` hub children (steering arm, axle and bush). Step 11: the gear rack with towball and both 6L steering links.
notes.interfaces: The parent places the axle at `0 -10 -120` with an identity matrix, so axle axes are frame axes. In axle coordinates the rack's toothed face is at y = −22 and the parent's pinion sits at y = −30, which matches the 10 LDU pitch radius of an 8T gear.
notes.parent_context: The front axle of the 8081 chassis (`8081 - Frame.ldr`).
notes.reuse_notes: Reuse it with its drive: copy the 8T pinion `3647` and its steering axle from the parent, or add an equivalent input. Without them the rack has nothing to move it. Keep the two hub children and the links together; they set the steering geometry.

guide.parent_supplies: The **8T pinion `3647`**, placed in `8081 - Frame.ldr` on the line after the axle. The isolated submodel has a rack and no pinion, which is the gap seen in the Technic car trial.
guide.corrected_description: A steerable, sprung front axle with a steering rack and links. It lacks the pinion, which the parent places.
guide.board_reading: Panel 1: the ghosted frame, with the axle highlighted. Panel 2: the isolated axle from the front, showing the symmetric arms, links and shock. Panels 3–4: source steps 6 (arms on the 1×6 brick) and 11 (rack and links). The isolated home view duplicates step 11, so the board leaves it out.
guide.limits: No view shows the teeth meshing; the mesh is a coordinate match only. Steering and suspension travel were not checked.

references.title: Differential rear axle with U-joints, mounted tilted

discovery.description: Rear axle assembly featuring a differential with bevel gears, universal joints, and a multi-link suspension structure.

notes.lesson: A driven Technic rear axle: a differential in an open frame, U-joints and half-shafts. The parent's matrix sets its tilt.
notes.construction: 63 parts in 8 evenly sized steps (6–12 placements each). Step 2: the differential with 12-tooth bevels. Step 3 (back view): the input double bevel and a U-joint enter the differential in its open 7×5 frame. Step 5: cross blocks and axles form the hub frames and outgoing half-shafts on both sides. Step 7: the shock absorber child.
notes.interfaces: The parent places it with matrix `-1 0 0 / 0 0.932 -0.363 / 0 -0.363 -0.932`: about 21° about X plus a half turn. The input U-joint takes the drive; the shock's top end anchors to the body.
notes.parent_context: The rear axle of `42075 - vehicle.ldr`, tilted under the rear, with the shock leaning up to the body.
notes.reuse_notes: Keep the differential frame, U-joint input and half-shafts together. Derive the tilt for the new chassis instead of copying the matrix: the tilt sets the input shaft angle. Replace the generated spring mesh with a real shock absorber part before reuse.

guide.parent_supplies: The tilted mount and the body anchor for the shock. The ghosted parent shows both.
guide.corrected_description: A rear axle with a bevel differential, universal joints and multi-link suspension.
guide.board_reading: Panel 1: the ghosted vehicle shows the tilt and the shock anchor. Panel 2: the isolated axle. Panel 3: source step 3 from the back, where the input bevel and U-joint enter the differential. Panel 4: step 5, hub frames and half-shafts.
guide.limits: Inspiration only: the shock child `42075 - shock-06_5L-hard-1.ldr` includes an LDCad-generated spring mesh made of raw polygons, which fails the source checks (`coverage.raw_geometry`). The Technic construction itself raised no errors. Suspension travel and U-joint angles were not checked.

references.title: V8 engine: crank train hidden under the cylinder banks

discovery.description: A Technic V-engine assembly with eight cylinder heads, pistons, connecting rods, and dual crankshafts mounted on a 5x3 brick base.

notes.lesson: A Technic V8 puts its whole crank train in one step between the two cylinder banks, so the finished engine hides it.
notes.construction: 70 parts in 8 steps. Steps 1–2: the 5×3 Technic brick frame and the first bank of four cylinders. Step 3: the whole crank train, with 8 pistons, 8 connecting rods, crankshaft ends and centres (26 placements). Step 4: the second bank closes over it. Steps 5–8: a second frame brick, cross block, liftarms, a 16-tooth gear and a T-beam. The 8 cylinder heads are embedded `42050 - 2850b.dat` parts.
notes.interfaces: The parent tilts it about 4° about X at the front of the car. Step 7 adds a 16-tooth gear; how the parent drives the crank was not traced.
notes.parent_context: The engine at the front of `42050 - Drag Racer.ldr`.
notes.reuse_notes: Build the crank train before closing the second bank. Keep the embedded cylinder definition with the source; the extracted `source.mpd` already carries it.

guide.parent_supplies: The 4° tilt and the engine's place at the front of the car.
guide.corrected_description: A Technic V-engine with eight cylinders, pistons, rods and crankshafts on a 5×3 brick base.
guide.board_reading: Panel 1: the ghosted drag racer from the right, engine highlighted. Panel 2: the finished engine; the crank is hidden. Panel 3: source step 3, the crank train going in. Panel 4: an x-ray copy where every placement outside step 3 is trans-clear. It shows two banks in a V over one crank, which no source view shows. X-ray works here because a thin shell covers a few distinctively coloured parts.
guide.limits: The crank was not turned, and piston clearance was not checked.

references.title: Slave I cockpit pod on a revolute pivot

discovery.description: Hinged structural platform with round snapstud plates, curved black slopes, and a Jedi Starfighter controls tile forming a cockpit or canopy base.

notes.lesson: A pilot pod turns on two pinned axles in Technic-brick bearings. The axis comes from connector data, not from the picture.
notes.construction: 50 parts in 13 steps. Step 1: a 4×4 round plate. Step 3: a 9-position locking hinge and plates. Step 9: four curved arches loop over the seat as the canopy frame. Step 11: liftarms with friction pins and blue axle pins. Step 13: 1×6 Technic bricks on both sides and the Boba Fett minifigure child.
notes.interfaces: The axle half of each `43093` sits in a `74695` liftarm pinned to the pod; the pin half turns in the centre hole of a `3894` brick. The axis runs through (0, −18, 0) along +Z in section coordinates, and through (0, −182, −300) along −X in the ship. The two bearing bricks are the fixed group; everything else moves.
notes.parent_context: The pilot pod inside the canopy dome of `75060 - main.ldr`, rotated 90° about Y, with Boba Fett tilted 15°.
notes.reuse_notes: Use the same pin-in-brick bearing for any pod that must stay level while a hull turns. Derive the axis from both connectors before marking or posing it.

guide.parent_supplies: The canopy dome around the pod, and the ship that turns about the lateral axis. You confirmed in review that the cockpit rotates.
guide.corrected_description: The pilot pod inside the canopy dome, on a pivot; not a generic hinged platform.
guide.board_reading: The main board: panel 1 is the ghosted ship, pod highlighted, with the neon-green pivot axis. Panel 2: source step 9, the canopy arches. Panel 3: the pivot hardware (pins and bearings) in magenta with the axis rod. Panel 4: the moving group turned 90° with the bearings fixed. The pose-sweep board renders 0°, 45° and 90° with one fixed camera in `analysis` mode, so its three panels compare directly. The three-pose sweep is the default for moving parts. How the pivot is marked, with xray layers on synthetic copies: a `highlight` layer on `part:43093|part:3894` outlines only the pivot hardware; an `axis` layer draws the neon-green rod (custom code 9008), thicker in ship coordinates in the parent view; a `pose` layer rotates the moving group about the axis with the bearings fixed. The recipes state the centre and direction explicitly; `./ldraw-xray axes` only proposes candidates.
guide.limits: Coaxial connectors prove the geometry only, not that the joint turns freely. No clearance against the dome was checked. The marker and posed copies are for rendering only. The tilted minifigure produces warnings, not errors.
guide.evidence:
How the axis was found, from connector data:

1. Take each joint part's connector from `./ldraw-agent part`. The `43093` axle runs along local X through its origin; the `3894` centre pin hole is at local (0, 10, 0), along local Z.
2. Map each connector into section coordinates with its placement line: point = position + R · local point; direction = R · local axis.
3. Check that all four lines coincide. The two pins (z = ±80) and the two holes (z = ±90) all lie on x = 0, y = −18, along ±Z, with 0.0 LDU offset.
4. The marker centre is their midpoint, (0, −18, 0).
5. For the parent, map the same line through the section placement: (0, −164, −300) with `0 0 −1 / 0 1 0 / 1 0 0` gives (0, −182, −300) along −X.
6. Each pose applies p′ = R(θ)·(p − centre) + centre and M′ = R(θ)·M to every part except the bearings.
